title: Photography: Out of Auto
subtitle: A field workbook
summary: Written for one camera and one habit: a superzoom with a 24 mm to 2000 mm lens, left on its bird-watching mode because the dials are confusing. It takes back the settings the camera was choosing for you, explaining why snow turns grey, why autofocus grabs the twig in front of the bird, and where a small sensor runs out of light. By the end you should be able to stand in a marsh at dusk and pick the shutter speed yourself.
